title: Planning
one_line_goal: Plan written, checked and approved by you; no app code yet
summary: Build the project's memory (the wiki) and a plan portal for you, before any Ferrum code. The plain-language portal is built and reviewed; it waits for your walkthrough and your approvals.

tasks.title: Save the starting documents
tasks.chain: Your brief and scoping answers are the ground truth → store them word for word, never edited → every later page can cite them.
tasks.check: Both files exist, are marked unchangeable, and their fingerprints are recorded.

tasks.title: Write five research notes
tasks.chain: Plans built from memory go stale → research the wiki method, Tauri and WebView2, measurement, the plan-app stack and related work, with dated sources → decisions rest on checked facts.
tasks.check: Five notes exist; every source has an access date and a checked or uncertain label.

tasks.title: Write the wiki rules and live status
tasks.chain: Many sessions and helpers edit the wiki → one rulebook (page shapes, fingerprints) plus a live status file → any session can pick up where the last one stopped.
tasks.check: The fingerprint script runs on the rulebook; Claude's instructions link to it; the status file has its required fields.

tasks.title: Describe the architecture and its parts
tasks.chain: The app has many parts with different trust levels → one page per part, saying what it talks to → security boundaries are visible before any code.
tasks.check: Every planned part has exactly one page; every link that crosses a trust level is marked.

tasks.title: Write the decisions and the risk register
tasks.chain: Choices and risks get forgotten → one page per decision (19 at the time; more were added later) and per risk, with likelihood, impact and response → we can always see why, and what could go wrong.
tasks.check: 19 decision pages at the time, each with all required sections (later decisions came after); every risk has likelihood, impact, response and an owning phase.

tasks.title: Write the research plan pages
tasks.chain: Ferrum is also a research project → questions, predictions, experiments, metrics and test workloads, linked to each other → nothing is measured without a reason.
tasks.check: Links agree in both directions; no page states a measured number.

tasks.title: Write phase pages, index and log
tasks.chain: Work spans nine phases and many sessions → a page per phase, an index of every page and a running log → you and Claude can find anything.
tasks.check: The index lists every page once; log headings follow the agreed format.

tasks.title: Check the whole wiki
tasks.chain: Hundreds of linked pages drift → run every rule by hand or script and fingerprint the raw files → work starts from a clean, tamper-evident base.
tasks.check: The check report shows zero errors; every raw file has a recorded fingerprint.

tasks.title: Install Node and record versions
tasks.chain: The plan app needs Node 24 → install it and record exact versions → builds can be repeated.
tasks.check: Node, npm and git versions saved; Node's major version is 24.

tasks.title: Create the plan app skeleton
tasks.chain: Loose versions break things later → create the web app with exact versions and three small feasibility tests → a stable base for the rest.
tasks.check: Install shows no version conflicts; type check, style check and build succeed; the feasibility tests pass.

tasks.title: Teach the app to read the wiki
tasks.chain: The app shows wiki pages → a reader that checks each page's header against the rules → bad pages are flagged, not shown wrongly.
tasks.check: Tests on sample pages pass; the real wiki loads with zero header errors.

tasks.title: Fingerprint pages exactly like the reference
tasks.chain: Approvals are tied to page fingerprints → compute them in the app exactly like the reference script → a changed page can never keep an old approval.
tasks.check: The app and the reference script give identical fingerprints on every test case.

tasks.title: Build the app's views and wiki check
tasks.chain: You need to see the plan, not raw files → dashboard, roadmap, architecture, decisions, risks and research views, plus an automatic wiki check → the plan is readable and checked.
tasks.check: Browser tests open every view on a production build with no errors.

tasks.title: Build the approvals store
tasks.chain: Approvals must not be lost or forged → a local-only store with safe writes, every approval state tested → no approval is silently wrong.
tasks.check: Tests cover every approval state; requests from other computers are refused.

tasks.title: Build the approval screens
tasks.chain: Approvals were first planned inside the app → approve, change and reject buttons with an outdated-page badge → later replaced: you now approve in Claude Code.
tasks.check: Unit tests: when an approved page changes, its approval shows as 'Approved, page edited since'. The old screens and their browser test were removed with v1.

tasks.title: Run the full plan-app test gate
tasks.chain: Each piece passed on its own → run every check together and save the output → proof the whole app works.
tasks.check: All checks pass in one run with zero wiki errors; output saved.

tasks.title: Portal v2, then your review
tasks.chain: You found v1 too technical → rebuild it as a read-only portal in plain words, fed by text Claude writes from the wiki → you review it and approve in Claude Code; Claude records each approval.
tasks.check: The portal check reports clean; your approvals for the P1 pages are recorded.

tasks.title: Close P0
tasks.chain: All checks pass and the pages are approved → you approve the phase exit in Claude Code → Claude pauses; P1 starts only when you explicitly say go.
tasks.check: Exit approval recorded; a gate entry in the log; work committed locally; no P1 work before your go.

test_gate.explanation: Every later phase builds on this plan → the portal's style checks, tests and build pass in one run, with the output saved → you read the portal and approve in Claude Code → only then does P1 start.

rows.proves: The portal's code is clean and consistent.
Wiki reader, fingerprints and approval states behave as specified.
Every tab works on a production build, reachable from this computer only.
The app and the reference script compute identical fingerprints.
You read every tab and popup and said what is unclear, until it reads clearly.
You answered or deferred each open question.
